fair_value.method: Blend of three sum-of-the-parts views on a corrected pro forma post-VAC basis: ~331M shares (249.97M at 7/31/26 + 14.81M ASM shares actually issued 8/28/26 + 65.85M VAC) and ~$0.885B net claims (~$0.75B net debt at close + up to $0.135B Ara preferred). Conservative cash-flow SOTP $6.3 (40%), peer-multiple SOTP $9.3 (35%), risked NAV $9.6 (25%), which gives ~$8.2.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Conservative cash-flow SOTP. Uranium: ~1.75M lb/yr at ~$85 realized, ~$40/lb all-in cost, so ~$80M EBITDA x 11x = $0.9B, plus US development assets $0.3B = $1.2B. VAC: 2027 EBITDA ~$75M (midpoint of the $60-90M defensible range; Sumter's $65-75M is a run-rate, not a 2027 group figure) x 15x = $1.125B. Rare earths: White Mesa REE + heavy-REE circuits $0.3B; ASM $0.15B; Donald 49% option $0.10B (Phase 1 pre-tax NPV8 is A$759M, not A$2.3B; FID still not taken); Vara Mada 20% x $1.8B NPV = $0.36B; Bahia $0.05B. Overhead -$0.3B. EV ~$2.98B minus $0.885B net claims = $2.1B / 331M sh.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Peer-multiple SOTP. Uranium platform $1.8B (~20x 2027 EBITDA, US producer peer multiples); REE/magnet platform $2.45B (VAC $1.4B + upstream REE/ASM/Donald/Vara Mada $1.05B, trimmed $0.05B for the smaller Donald Phase 1 NPV); overhead -$0.3B. EV $3.95B minus $0.885B net claims = $3.07B / 331M sh.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Risked NAV using company project economics: Vara Mada $1.8B NPV x 35% = $0.63B; Donald 49% x A$759M Phase 1 pre-tax NPV8 x 0.7 after tax x 40% risk plus a small Phase 2 option = ~$0.10B; uranium NAV $1.5B; VAC at deal cost marked to today's price, as EV: $718M cash + 65.85M sh x $11.35 ($0.75B) + $0.135B preferred + $0.14B VAC net debt = $1.74B; White Mesa REE/ASM $0.5B; overhead -$0.3B. EV ~$4.17B minus $0.885B net claims minus ~$0.1B for future capex dilution (cut from $0.2B because the share count is now right) = ~$3.19B / 331M sh. Round 1's $12.0 had an arithmetic error: the listed components summed to ~$4.1B, not $5.0B.

bear.story: Uranium eases toward the $70s and White Mesa campaigns stay lumpy. The German FDI review drags the VAC close past Q1 2027 or adds constraining conditions (Hanau jobs, tech-transfer limits, EU supply priority). The deal closes with the $135M preferred kicker and 65.85M shares to a 19.9% holder who is an overhang. The $725M OSC loan is not finalized, so REE capex ($104M Phase 1B/1C and heavy-REE circuits) is funded by ATM or a discounted raise. Donald FID slips again, Madagascar stalls, and the US-China thaw keeps the rare-earth scarcity premium deflated.

base.story: Uranium holds $85-95, with 2027 sales of ~1.5-2M lb at high margins. VAC closes in H1 2027 with manageable German conditions. 2027 VAC EBITDA of ~$60-90M leaves the group around break-even after overhead and integration. The OSC loan is finalized in some form, and the heavy-REE circuit stays on track for late 2027. The stock trades around a blended SOTP of $8-12 with some residual strategic premium.

bull.story: A US/allied policy shock (renewed Chinese export controls, DoD price floors, Section 232 on magnets) re-rates Western mine-to-magnet platforms. The OSC loan is finalized, Donald reaches FID, Vara Mada's investment agreement is signed, and terbium/dysprosium qualification with Japanese magnet makers turns into contracts. Uranium runs above $100, and the stock revisits the $20-28 region, near analyst targets ($16-33).

thesis_break_reason: At ~$6 the pro forma equity is ~$2.0B (331M sh). Adding ~$0.885B of net claims gives an EV of ~$2.9B, below even my conservative cash-flow SOTP ($2.98B EV). The market would be assigning roughly zero value to the upstream REE platform, or pricing VAC at a steep discount to its cost. Before the VAC close, $6 x ~265M pre-VAC shares = ~$1.6B, about cash plus the uranium business. A move there would most likely mean something fundamental broke: the VAC close failed or was re-cut, the OSC loan fell through and forced a large discounted raise, uranium fell below ~$65/lb, or White Mesa had operating failures. With 70-90% vol this level is reachable by noise alone, so I would treat it as broken only on a sustained close there.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor established that my share count was ~5M short: ASM consideration was 14,808,572 EF shares issued on 8/28/26, which I confirmed in the 8-K, so pro forma is ~331M, not 326M. Net claims at the VAC close are ~$0.75B net debt plus up to $0.135B preferred (~$0.885B), not ~$0.8B. I accept both. Re-checking my own work also turned up two errors of mine. (1) The risked-NAV method's listed components summed to ~$4.1B EV, not the $5.0B I wrote, so that method falls from $12.0 to ~$9.6 even before the corrections. The fix is to value VAC as EV at today's deal cost ($1.74B) and cut the dilution haircut to $0.1B, as the supervisor suggested, to avoid double counting. (2) Donald: Astron's Phase 1 pre-tax NPV8 is A$759M. The A$2.3B figure is combined Phase 1+2, and FID is still not taken after two slips, so I trimmed the Donald value in every method. I also cut 2027 VAC EBITDA from $80M to $75M, inside the supervisor's $60-90M range. New evidence: Germany's Economy Ministry has a formal FDI review of VAC open, with conditions expected but no block. The late-September drop was sector-wide and tied to the US-China thaw deflating the scarcity premium. H.C. Wainwright lifted its target to $29.25 (Sept 1), and terbium oxide qualified with a Japanese magnet maker. The blended fair value falls from $9.3 to ~$8.2, lower than the supervisor's ~$9.1 re-run for me, mainly because of the NAV arithmetic fix. I disagree slightly with the supervisor's view that the corrections are too small to move the ladder: for me the combined changes are ~12% on fair value. I still do not put the median at fair value, because the market persistently pays a strategic policy premium for Western REE names, sell-side targets ($16-33) sit far above, and uranium fundamentals are strong. So I moved the lognormal median from ~$10.2 to ~$9.9 and kept sigma ~0.68 (below the 89% realized vol, which included one-off policy spikes). I trimmed the far-left tail for financing-crash risk. P(>= $11.35) is 0.42, and the scenario mean is ~$11.0. No option data or priors were used.
